expectations.text: Output contains a markdown table with Requirement, Status, and Evidence columns
expectations.evidence: Has two tables: 'Requirements Coverage' (Requirement | Covered? | Notes) and 'Edge Cases & Gaps' (Gap | Severity | Status). Column names don't match the expected format.

expectations.text: At least 5 distinct requirements are identified in the audit (explicit + implied)
expectations.evidence: 4 explicit requirements in coverage table + 10 gaps in edge case table + 5 implied requirements section = well over 5 distinct requirements identified.

expectations.text: Every 'Covered' status has a specific citation (section name or quote), not vague references
expectations.evidence: Coverage table uses brief notes like 'Existing handler routes to entry, subscription, or one-time payment' but doesn't cite specific plan section names or quote plan text.

expectations.text: Output includes a numerical coverage score between 0-100
expectations.evidence: No numerical coverage score present anywhere in the output.

expectations.text: At least 1 requirement is marked Partial or Missing
expectations.evidence: 10 gaps identified in the 'Edge Cases & Gaps' table, including HIGH severity items like 'No idempotency protection', 'Edge Function location mismatch', and 'Webhook endpoint not registered in Stripe'.

expectations.text: Output includes a patched plan section that addresses identified gaps
expectations.evidence: Gaps are listed with severity and status references to plan phases, but there's no explicit 'patched plan' section that updates the original plan with fixes.

expectations.text: Surfaces non-obvious requirements like webhook signature verification, idempotency handling, retry logic, or event ordering
expectations.evidence: Surfaces idempotency (HIGH), race conditions on customer record creation (MEDIUM), webhook secret rotation, Stripe response time requirements, pro tier mapping gap, and retry logic.

eval_feedback.overall: Baseline lacks structured format (expected, since no skill was used) but excels at finding real gaps. Found more actionable issues than the with-skill version.
